# 📅 Calendar Window

**Connor's real Outlook calendar for the next ~3 weeks. Generated by Phase 1 of the refresh — never hand-edited.**

generated: 2026-11-13 18:33 ET
window: 2026-11-13 → 2026-12-03
source: Outlook, Connor's default calendar (M365 connector `outlook_calendar_search`, 55 events, self-blocks excluded). Never Google Calendar.
pulled_by: grace-quick-refresh

> **Read this before writing any sentence of the form "raise it at X," "bring it to X," or "wait for X."** The occasion is a fact, not a framing. This file exists because on 2026-08-20 a refresh report told Connor to raise a stalled item with John Slye "at the Mon 8/24 session" — 8/24 is Kay's PCO/Rock tutorial with Kay, Jennifer and Connor. John is not on it, and no occasion existed before that item's 9/6 `needs_by` where the two of them were on the same call. See [[Changelog/2026-08-20-calendar-window]].
>
> Query it, don't skim it: `python3 "Workflows/calendar-window.py" --who "John Slye" --before 2026-09-06`.

**Excluded deliberately:** the daily self-blocks `Morning Availability`, `Afternoon Availability` and `Daily FTJ Conflict`. Connor puts those on his own calendar to shape availability — they are **not meetings**, they have no attendees, and reporting one as an occasion to raise something at would be the same error this file exists to prevent. `calendar-window.py` drops them again by subject as a second line of defence.
